title: Von Thomas Next
description: A real catering operations system with customer offers, pricing logic, admin repair tools, payment follow-up, and local SEO pages.
body:
Von Thomas Next is the working web and operations system behind a real catering business. It helps visitors understand the offer, send better requests, and move from interest to a clear catering proposal. It also gives the team admin tools for pricing, documents, orders, payments, and kitchen handoff.

The project matters because catering is full of small details. A customer may ask for a buffet, finger food, lunch catering, or a bigger event. The team needs guest counts, dates, delivery details, food choices, equipment, payment status, and confirmation timing. If those details live only in messages, work becomes slow and mistakes become easy.

## What it does

- Lets customers explore catering offers and request a proposal online.
- Helps turn menu choices and guest counts into clearer offers.
- Supports admin review, pricing repair, order overview, and operational follow-up.
- Handles separate delivery and billing addresses.
- Improves payment follow-up and deposit handling.
- Supports local service pages so people can find the right catering page for their city and intent.
- Gives the team better visibility into inquiries, emails, and order state.

## Recent work

The June work focused on making the offer flow more dependable. The offer system gained a pricing engine and regression tests, admin pricing repair guards, better package carryover logic, a Tuesday cutoff for confirmations, and fixes for buffet guidance blockers. Proposal dialogs and menu image variants were improved so customers can make choices with less confusion.

The operations side also moved forward. Payment polling replaced a fragile webhook path, invoice repair and audit reports were added, monthly tax export support was built, and the order overview gained an auto-cancellation switch. The admin system now links Chef-Culinar alerts to orders, stores offer attribution click IDs, and supports separate billing and delivery addresses.

Search and performance work continued too. The homepage gallery images and Core Web Vitals were improved, service-city content was refreshed, indexation issues were fixed, and admin delivery edits became safer.

## Value for users

For customers, the value is a clearer path from “I need catering” to “I can ask for a good offer.” For the catering team, the value is fewer manual checks, fewer missing details, and more confidence before an order moves into preparation.

## Current direction

The current direction is operational trust. The system should make the right price easier to reach, show the right status to admins, and reduce the number of edge cases that need manual repair.

## Public boundary

This page explains the product and public build direction. It does not include private customer records, supplier terms, internal reports, credentials, or financial data.
